evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Apply data validation, monitoring and quality controls to ensure reliable, trusted and maintainable data foundations
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Responsibilities center on data validation, quality controls, governance, and compliance with no velocity/speed language present.
evidence.domain_risk: 5+ year data engineering, analytics engineering, software engineering, data management or related fields, preferably supporting analytics or AI use cases in the finance domain
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Financial Analytics data products for a pharmaceutical company's finance function carry regulatory and financial-reporting implications, placing this at high domain risk.
evidence.collaboration_width: Financial Analytics Product Managers; Data Scientists; Global DX
evidence.data_team_maturity: Collaborate with Financial Analytics Product Managers, Data Scientists, Global DX and technical teams to align solutions with enterprise architecture, engineering standards and delivery requirements
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: Named sub-teams (Global DX, Financial Analytics Product Managers) and enterprise architecture/engineering standards imply an established, mature data organization.
evidence.jd_authorship: Design, develop and maintain scalable data pipelines, transformation logic, reusable datasets and data products for Financial Analytics use cases
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Specific technical scope (transformation logic, data validation, operationalization) is mixed with generic corporate boilerplate about the company's mission and equal-opportunity statement.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: translate analytical and product requirements into scalable data and analytics products for Financial Analytics use cases
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The role is explicitly built around a Financial Analytics function, naming Financial Analytics Product Managers as the primary collaborator.
evidence.autonomy_level: supporting data integration, transformation, operationalization and delivery activities
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: Responsibilities are framed as supporting and delivering against requirements defined by product managers and data scientists, not setting direction.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: AI is mentioned only as a use case the role may support ('supporting analytics or AI use cases in the finance domain'), not as a skill or tool the candidate is expected to use.
evidence.testing_framing: Apply data validation, monitoring and quality controls to ensure reliable, trusted and maintainable data foundations
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Data validation and quality controls are framed as an owned responsibility with an action verb ('apply'), not just listed as a skill.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: Apply data validation, monitoring and quality controls to ensure reliable, trusted and maintainable data foundations
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: High — reliability, trust, monitoring, and compliance with data governance/security standards are named repeatedly across the responsibility list.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: development, operation and continuous improvement of data products and analytical capabilities
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Mix of new development and continuous improvement/operation of existing data products.
evidence.loss_aversion: Apply data validation, monitoring and quality controls to ensure reliable, trusted and maintainable data foundations — reflects strong operational/compliance risk framing tied to financial analytics data.
